The funny details make it ours.Come alongAn afternoonwithout much plot.York made it into our camera roll through a view, some sea air and a lobster-shaped sweet. The Nubble can be the destination without becoming a list of things to finish.Looking for practical details? From our family notebook · York, MaineThe view arrives first.York is very good at reminding us that an outing does not need a narrative arc. Sometimes the entire story is: we drove to the coast, we saw the ocean, somebody got an absurd Maine-shaped sweet, we looked at a lighthouse, and everyone went home with salt in their hair and the agreeable tiredness that comes from having actually been somewhere.The Nubble works especially well because so much of the pleasure arrives immediately. You do not have to hike for an hour before you earn the view. There it is: rock, water, white lighthouse, red roof, gulls doing what gulls do, and the ocean making everything else seem temporarily less important. You can stay a long time or a short time and the basic experience is still intact.The original family story is retained from the earlier notebook; the decorative artwork is an interpretation.Check the weather, the facilities and the way back.More from our York notebook +We like places where the person who wants to look can look, the person who wants to move can move, and the person who is ready to get back in the car has not ruined a carefully choreographed plan. York has enough around it to build a whole day, but it does not require one. That distinction has saved many family outings.The photograph we kept from York is not a formal lighthouse portrait. It is a small, funny family moment with a lobster-shaped sweet, which feels exactly right. The landmark gives the day its setting; the odd little details make it ours. That is what we are trying to preserve in these Favorite Places—not just where to go, but why the place stayed with us. Sometimes the souvenir is the absurd sweet.The details that stayedWhat the camera roll remembers.There are also small pleasures that become disproportionately memorable. A silly candy. Setup: Does it need tools, charging, a separate purchase or an account?Upkeep: Who will wash it, store it, refill it or replace the parts?Ongoing cost: Does useful access require a membership, app payment or regular supplies?Fit: Is there space for it, and can the recipient use its controls and packaging?Flexibility: Can it be exchanged, returned or used at another time?
